original_question: Which projective varieties M in projective space P^n have maximum likelihood degree 1, meaning that for generic data vector (u0, u1, ..., un) the restriction of the likelihood function L(p0, p1, ..., pn) = p0^u0 · p1^u1 · ... · pn^un / (p0 + p1 + ··· + pn)^(u0 + u1 + ··· + un) to M has exactly one complex critical point after excluding singular points of M and points where L has poles or zeros?
target_in_paper: The concrete open problem in the paper's Maximum Likelihood part: characterize all projective varieties whose maximum likelihood degree is equal to one.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right target problem and stays close to the paper's intent. It correctly asks for a characterization of projective varieties with maximum likelihood degree 1, uses the same projective likelihood function L on coordinates (p0:...:pn), assumes generic data, and excludes points where the likelihood has poles or zeros. It also correctly interprets ML degree 1 as having exactly one complex critical point for generic data.
missing_details: The paper works with projective coordinates (p0:...:pn) on projective space P^n, so the ambient setting should be stated explicitly as a projective subvariety M ⊂ P^n over C.
The data vector is not arbitrary: it is taken as u=(u0,...,un) in N^(n+1), with genericity understood in the algebraic-geometric sense (outside a proper algebraic subset of the data space).
It is worth stating that L_u is a well-defined rational function on P^n because the numerator and denominator are homogeneous of the same total degree u0+...+un.
The paper calls such M an algebraic statistical model, i.e. a subvariety of P^n; that terminology is part of the nearby context.

Critical points should be understood on the smooth locus of M; your draft says this implicitly by excluding singular points, but the paper's official statement leaves this implicit in the phrase 'critical points of the restriction'.

The statistical motivation identifies the probability simplex with the nonnegative part of projective space P^n_{>=0}; this is nearby context in the paper, even though the ML degree itself is counted over C.
The paper states this as a characterization problem over all projective spaces, not as a fixed-n classification or as a search for examples.

The paper mentions, but does not solve, a broader neighboring question about the geometry of maximum likelihood estimation and possible relations to EM convergence; that broader question should not be merged into the refined statement.
refined_question: Characterize all complex projective subvarieties M ⊂ P^n (for arbitrary n), with projective coordinates (p0:...:pn), whose maximum likelihood degree is 1; that is, determine exactly which algebraic statistical models M have the property that for Zariski-generic data u=(u0,...,un) ∈ N^(n+1), the rational function L_u(p)=p0^u0 p1^u1 ··· pn^un /(p0+...+pn)^(u0+...+un), which is homogeneous of degree 0 and hence well defined on P^n, has exactly one complex critical point when restricted to the smooth locus of M away from the zero/pole divisor of L_u.
justification: The draft clearly targets the paper's concrete Maximum Likelihood open problem rather than the neighboring general discussion. The paper states the problem tersely as 'Characterize all projective varieties whose maximum likelihood degree is equal to one,' and the immediately following pages define the projective likelihood function, the role of the generic data vector u ∈ N^(n+1), and the convention that only critical points that are not poles or zeros are counted. The refined version therefore keeps the characterization framing, adds the ambient complex projective setting and projective-coordinate notation from the surrounding context, and makes explicit the smooth-locus interpretation of 'critical point' that is implicit in the paper. I did not broaden the question to EM convergence or to later characterizations via discriminants/Horn uniformization, because those are not the actual target statement of this 2007 paper. I also did not include a separate alternate formulation in terms of rational MLE, since the paper only illustrates that equivalence by example here rather than stating it as the official formulation.
